body:
Closes #52.

The Visits grid now loads one page at a time from the server, in pages of 5, 10 or 20 rows, and every column (Date, Description, Pet, Owner) can be sorted by clicking its header. It opens on the 10 newest visits. The page, size and sort stay in the URL, so Back, refresh and bookmarks restore the same view.

The decision a reviewer most needs to know is that paging runs on the server. That breaks the API: `GET /api/visits` now returns a page object instead of a bare array. It takes `page`, `size` (1–100) and `sort` (`date|description|pet|owner`, then `,asc` or `,desc`), and answers 400 to anything else. This follows the owners-grid paging from #25. Ties on the sorted column are broken newest first, then by id, so no visit appears on two pages or on none. Two things are left open. No index backs the default date sort, so `visits(visit_date, id)` is the follow-up if the table grows. The new e2e test "a page of 5 visits, then the next one" is flaky: it reads its expected rows from the API while parallel suites add visits to the same database.


Opened for the review demo, do not merge.
